intel.text: The call is a recruiting call: Rob is signing David as MLE's first outside sales rep. 'If you were the first person to come on and do this, you would be the first sales rep of mine, like, and I can't have the first sales rep not work.'
Rep compensation as stated to David: 'you'll get your part of the of the up of the one time fee, the setup fee, and as well, you'll get your, you know, your monthly recurring revenue in perpetuity.'

The four-phase offer, laid out end to end: phase 1 = AI/SEO/GEO/convertibility-optimised website + a self-updating 'second brain'; phase 2 = the automations marketplace ('50,000 automations'), priced per automation, e.g. '$2,000 upfront and $300 a month' or '$5,000 and $4,000 a month'; phase 3 = bespoke build after a full business audit; phase 4 = 'we actually partner with you' — a new entity.

Real-estate brokerage closed the day before this call at '$18,000' flat for a up-to-2,000-page MLS website + 60 agent pages + a company second brain + per-agent second brains + automated social posting with AI avatar video. Rob's own comparison: five frontier models priced the same scope at 'about $2,000,000 upfront and $400,000 a month'.
Website + second brain has no list price: 'I've charged guys $18,000 for them. I've charged $500 for them. Right? It it just it it all depends. Get what you can get.'

Two customer-facing guarantees are made on this call. Views: 'We can guarantee a million views within the first month.' Refund: 'Within thirty days of us delivering these products, if you don't like it, you don't wanna move forward, you don't see any value to it, we will give you a full refund, and you get to keep the tech' — repeated for phase 2 ('another thirty days later... you keep all the tech, and we'll give you the refund for what you've paid to date').

Two 50/50 partnerships stated as agreed on deals closed the day before: with the roofer, on a roofing production+CRM software that 'just doesn't exist' — 'we're like, okay. Yeah. We'll go fifty fifty on that'; and with the real-estate principal, on further ventures — 'he has, like, two other ones... that he's just gonna, you know, give us $50.50 on.'

The real-estate software being partnered on is a BoomTown displacement. 'It's called BoomTown, and they charge $2,500 a month... You can't build on top of it. They don't offer API stuff... only 20% tops of the things that real estate agents and brokerages actually need does BoomTown offer.' 'So Alex has already been building out this this CRM, and it looked good. So we're like, okay. Let's partner on that.'

Rob's stated volume when asked how many businesses: 'About a 100, and then we're about to sign up 18,000.' The 18,000 is one of the partner's former clients rolling out to its own B2B base — 'they have 18,000 clients. They're all rolling it all out soon.'

The technical partner is named as Will, 25, 'been working on AI since he's been eight years old', and his prior technologies are claimed as 'implemented in 17,000 companies and generated an additional $11,000,000,000 in revenue'; 'through Will's collective, technologies, they've been used by over 17,000 clients.' Rob qualifies the number himself: 'to be candid, not necessarily a lot of it wasn't related to this venture.'

Qualia named as a white-label target with an existing relationship: 'In real estate, there's a big home closing company called Qualia. They do about 60 percent of all home closings... we're gonna actually go into Qualia because we have a relationship with them.' Rob frames the open question as white-label vs branded: 'should I allow Qualia to white label all of our automations, or should I let a bunch of different providers in the industry offer our automations but still show that it's us.'

A Canada white-label deal is in flight and priced: 'my partner's flying up and talking with one of his old customers in, Canada, and they want to white label it for their 20,000 customers. We wouldn't even think about doing that for less than high high seven figures.'

What David brings: a payment-processing merchant portfolio and the trust that comes with it. Rob's own framing of why that matters — 'Payment processing is great because unless you've really fucked up as a payment processor, they stay with you for a long time.'

David names his own first candidate: 'They're called fruit truck... 3 or $400,000 a month doing these farmers markets.' He is their processor — 'I take care of all of the processing' — and knows the owners personally.

Second candidate named: 'a company called US Card Solutions. I've got some accounts with them... they just recently became a full service provider. So they have all in house underwriting. They ride the rails of Fiserv.' David is 'good friends with the owner of the company' (line 413).

David's stated weekend homework and his own segment pick: 'I'm gonna be working this weekend through my client base and finding markets... I'm gonna be looking at going after franchises with this this opportunity.'

Mark — David's partner, not on this call — is running an ISO roll-up: 'our strategy is definitely a roll up... buy ISOs... wrapping things into a PayFac... Mark wants to get, like, 50 to 100,000,000.' Rob's position on Mark is explicitly reserved: 'my relationship with Mark is such that I don't know Mark very well... if you guys are able to spin up capital to help acquire processing companies, like, I'm in... But I don't really know him beyond that.'

Rob declines the funding conversation outright: 'money is the last thing we need. We don't need any money. I mean, we've got people that wanna throw us tons of money right now. We have Fidelity who wants to open up a billion dollar line of credit for it. We don't wanna do that.' RECORDED VERBATIM AND NOT ASSERTED — this read makes no claim about any Fidelity facility.

A payments idea is raised and deliberately not explained: 'I can't get into it right now, but I also thought of a way to usurp... a not insignificant portion of Stripe's customers where they would wanna come to us before Stripe. I figured out a way to do it.' Said at 2026-07-09 or earlier — i.e. BEFORE the 2026-07-25 payments-layer dump that became Q60/Q61.

Roofing sales-rep retention, from Rob's coaching years: 'in the roofing industry, this is broadly in the trades, only about 30% of the sales reps that you hire are both with the company a year later and are hitting their KPIs... With this test, we got it to 92%.' The instrument named is OMG, tailored first to roofing and then per-company.

Exit-multiple argument, used live on a roofer: 'Analyzed 150 roofing companies and the biggest difference in what kind of multiple they were paid for was companies that had a lower percentage of owner dependency or single rep dependency and those that had a good tech stack in place.' Worked example given to the owner: $10M revenue, 10% EBITDA, '4x versus 7x' — 'me putting this system in place for you just made this business, when you sell it, an extra $3,000,000.'

Rob's account of the coaching company he left: 'I just did not have much aligned with them ethically at all... They cheated me out of a lot of money.' Amount, when David asks: 'Oh, man. 50, 60... if you go all in, over a 100 across various things. And I'll never see that.' THE COMPANY IS NEVER NAMED IN THIS TRANSCRIPT and is not named here either.

Cold-canvass proof point offered as the sales motion: 'one day, we just walked up and down 5th Street here and signed up 29 of the 30 businesses.' Delivery speed stated twice: 'it takes us about forty minutes to spin up the second brain and the website if they wanna move forward to get it live. It only takes about twenty minutes.'

Rob's commitment, made three times: send David the recording/transcript so he can work it through ChatGPT against his own portfolio — 'I'll send you the transcript of this conversation for you to really do your due diligence. Look at your portfolio. Think about the customers that you already have, and then come back to me.'

Agreed follow-up: 'We'll bounce in a call next week or something' (Rob, line 395) and 'We'll talk Monday' (David, line 429), with Rob inviting weekend contact — 'feel free to shoot me over any text message over the weekend. I work seven days a week.'

David asks for enablement Rob has not built: 'You already have bullet points? So, like, if I call on a franchise...' — answered with 'Bro, you'll be able to get it from this conversation.' Rob does name the intended fix: 'one of the things I'm gonna do is set up, like, some type of knowledge base or chatbot' a rep can query on fit.

P-1020's CRM description already reads 'Very Excited to get training and onboarding. We need more Social Proof and Mini Case Studies first which I communicated to Will' — which this call is the source conversation for, and which the CRM records with no date, no activity and no link to this transcript.
